speaker_role: former admissions officer (former director of admissions at Swarthmore College, former admissions officer at Vanderbilt University)
commercial_incentive: yes -- repeatedly promotes his paid junior application materials review service, a parents' course, and website askdrhoffman.com
key_insights: Recommends skipping study hall, early release, late arrival, or graduating early where possible, since colleges evaluate how far a student pushed themselves academically rather than how quickly they could finish
Advises limiting how widely a student shares their college list, test scores, and decision plans to avoid unnecessary social comparison and pressure
Notes some colleges track engagement signals like opening/clicking admissions emails and portal login frequency as demonstrated interest, and recommends identifying which target schools track this
Recommends prioritizing net price calculators over sticker price when building a college list, since actual aid-adjusted cost is what matters financially

Advises diversifying recommendation letters across subject areas (e.g., one humanities, one science teacher) but staying within or just one letter over the school's stated limit, since excess letters can dilute rather than strengthen an application
States that activity order/placement on the application matters ('admissions real estate') and can affect how the file is perceived
Recommends reporting AP scores of 4s and 5s (and sometimes passing 3s depending on context) since colleges let applicants choose which scores to self-report
Advises proofreading the generated Common App PDF specifically, since that PDF (not the live portal) is what admissions readers actually see, and formatting errors can surface only in that version
Recommends fee waivers are available broadly (not only for low-income families) across application, testing, and CSS Profile fees
Advises treating optional interviews as effectively not optional, since they add personality/context to a file
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker recommends writing one supplemental essay per week from when supplements are confirmed through deadlines
Speaker notes summer program deadlines can be as early as November, with many clustering in January-February
notable_or_distinctive: Extremely dense checklist format (50 items) covering operational/tactical details rarely mentioned elsewhere, such as proofreading the generated Common App PDF specifically and treating recommendation letters as subject to a 'too many can dilute' effect.
reliability_notes: Heavy repeated self-promotion of paid services (application review, parents' course) throughout; despite genuine former-admissions-officer credentials, several claims (e.g., specific demonstrated-interest tracking behaviors, AP score reporting norms) are generalized advice that varies significantly by individual college policy.
